items.stem: Define the term 'stakeholder'.
items.answer: Any individual or group that has an interest in, or is affected by, the activities of a business.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – Any individual or group that has an interest in, or is affected by, the activities of a business. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain the difference between a stakeholder and a shareholder.
items.answer: A shareholder owns part of a company; a stakeholder is anyone with an interest in or affected by the business, which includes shareholders but also employees, customers and the community.
items.markingKey: 1 mark shareholder = owner; 1 mark stakeholder broader with example. [2]

items.stem: Explain the objectives of two different stakeholder groups.
items.answer: Employees want job security, good pay and working conditions; customers want good quality products at fair prices with good service.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark group, 1 mark objective explained). [4]

items.stem: World cocoa prices have doubled in eighteen months. Gold Coast Cocoa Ltd, a private limited company in Ghana with about 450 employees, buys cocoa from local co-operatives and makes premium chocolate bars. Explain how the local community could be affected by the expansion of Gold Coast Cocoa.
items.answer: Points to develop for Gold Coast Cocoa: the community is an external stakeholder; more jobs and income locally; more traffic, noise or pollution; demand for local suppliers rises.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: the community is an external stakeholder. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Gold Coast Cocoa (confectionery). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. more jobs and income locally; more traffic, noise or pollution. [3]

items.stem: Bosphorus Home AŞ is a public limited company based in Istanbul, Turkey. It makes washing machines, fridges and ovens sold in Europe and the Middle East and employs about 3,500 people. Inflation in Turkey has been above 40% for two years. Explain how the local community could be affected by the expansion of Bosphorus Home.
items.answer: Points to develop for Bosphorus Home: the community is an external stakeholder; more jobs and income locally; more traffic, noise or pollution; demand for local suppliers rises.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: the community is an external stakeholder. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Bosphorus Home (household appliance manufacturing). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. more jobs and income locally; more traffic, noise or pollution. [3]

items.stem: Siam Ready Meals is a private limited company in Bangkok, Thailand with about 1,100 staff. It produces chilled and frozen ready meals for supermarkets and convenience stores. Its biggest customer, a convenience-store chain, wants deliveries twice a day. Evaluate which stakeholder group is most important to Siam Ready Meals.
items.answer: For: shareholders/owners provide capital and control; customers provide revenue; employees produce the ready meals. Against: importance changes with the decision; all are interdependent; legal duties to some groups. Judgement: for Siam Ready Meals it depends mainly on the decision being made, and also on the legal structure.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts. AO2 Application [2]: uses the evidence (Siam Ready Meals: food manufacturing, about 1,100 employees, private limited company in Thailand; its biggest customer, a convenience-store chain, wants deliveries twice a day). AO3 Analysis [3]: arguments for, e.g. shareholders/owners provide capital and control; customers provide revenue; employees produce the ready meals; arguments against, e.g. importance changes with the decision; all are interdependent; legal duties to some groups. AO4 Evaluation [3]: a justified judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on the decision being made; the legal structure; the power of each group. A top-level answer reaches a supported conclusion specific to Siam Ready Meals. [10]

items.stem: Which stakeholder is most interested in a business's ability to repay a loan?
items.answer: A bank
items.markingKey: A bank. Lenders want repayment with interest. [1]

items.stem: Deccan Auto Components Ltd is a public limited company based in Mumbai, India. It supplies brakes and steering parts to car manufacturers and employs about 2,200 people. Its car-maker customers are switching rapidly to electric vehicles. Identify and explain one disadvantage for Deccan Auto of taking account of all stakeholders in its decisions.
items.answer: Decisions are slower; this would be a problem for Deccan Auto, which supplies brakes and steering parts to car manufacturers.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: relevant disadvantage, e.g. decisions are slower; may reduce profit for shareholders; impossible to satisfy everyone. 1 mark: explained in the context of Deccan Auto (automotive components). [2]

items.answer: Better reputation; this would help Petra Prints, which prints leaflets, posters and packaging for local businesses.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: relevant advantage, e.g. better reputation; more loyal customers and staff; fewer conflicts with the community. 1 mark: explained in the context of Petra Prints (printing). [2]

items.answer: (a) A stakeholder who is part of the business, such as an employee, manager or owner. (b) Better reputation.

items.stem: Define the term 'stakeholder conflict'.
items.answer: A situation where the objectives of different stakeholder groups cannot all be met at the same time.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – A situation where the objectives of different stakeholder groups cannot all be met at the same time. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain one example of conflict between the objectives of two stakeholder groups.
items.answer: Shareholders want lower costs to raise profits, while the local community wants the business to install expensive pollution controls; both cannot be fully satisfied.
items.markingKey: 1 mark two groups and objectives; 1 mark why they conflict. [2]

items.stem: Explain how a business might resolve a conflict between its stakeholders.
items.answer: Managers can consult the groups, negotiate a compromise (for example a smaller pay rise linked to productivity), and use stakeholder mapping to prioritise the most powerful groups.
items.markingKey: 1 mark consultation/negotiation; 1 mark compromise example; 1 mark prioritise. [3]

items.answer: Points to develop for Blue Lagoon Tours: conflict occurs when objectives clash; consultation and communication of plans; compromise such as reducing noise or creating local jobs; CSR initiatives to rebuild trust.

items.stem: Define the term 'stakeholder mapping'.
items.answer: A way of analysing stakeholders according to their power to influence a business and their interest in its decisions.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – A way of analysing stakeholders according to their power to influence a business and their interest in its decisions. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain how a business would use a stakeholder map when planning a new factory.
items.answer: It would place each stakeholder on a grid by power and interest, then involve key players closely, keep powerful groups satisfied and keep interested groups informed.
items.markingKey: 1 mark power and interest grid; 1 mark action for key players; 1 mark action for other groups. [3]

items.stem: Explain one limitation of stakeholder mapping.
items.answer: The power and interest of stakeholders change over time and are judged subjectively by managers, so the map may become inaccurate.
items.markingKey: 1 mark limitation; 1 mark explanation. [2]

items.answer: Points to develop for Indus Sports: stakeholder mapping uses power and interest; identifies key players such as major customers or investors; plans how to keep powerful groups satisfied; reduces the risk of opposition delaying the launch.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: stakeholder mapping uses power and interest. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Indus Sports (sports equipment manufacturing). items.stem: Based in Seoul, Han River Games Co. (private limited company) develops mobile games that earn revenue from in-game purchases. The business has around 340 employees. One game earns 70% of its revenue and its popularity is starting to fall. Explain the objectives of two stakeholder groups of Han River Games.
items.answer: Points to develop for Han River Games: stakeholders have different interests in the business; employees seek pay and job security; shareholders or owners seek profit and growth; customers want quality mobile games at fair prices.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: stakeholders have different interests in the business. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Han River Games (video game development). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. employees seek pay and job security; shareholders or owners seek profit and growth. [4]

items.stem: Atlas Furniture plc is a public limited company based in Alexandria, Egypt. It makes furniture and sells it through 40 stores and employs about 1,300 people. Sales in its stores have fallen while online sales have grown. Evaluate which stakeholder group is most important to Atlas Furniture.
items.answer: For: shareholders/owners provide capital and control; customers provide revenue; employees produce the furniture. Against: importance changes with the decision; all are interdependent; legal duties to some groups. Judgement: for Atlas Furniture it depends mainly on the decision being made, and also on the legal structure.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts. AO2 Application [2]: uses the evidence (Atlas Furniture: furniture manufacturing and retail, about 1,300 employees, public limited company in Egypt; sales in its stores have fallen while online sales have grown). AO3 Analysis [3]: arguments for, e.g. shareholders/owners provide capital and control; customers provide revenue; employees produce the furniture; arguments against, e.g. importance changes with the decision; all are interdependent; legal duties to some groups. AO4 Evaluation [3]: a justified judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on the decision being made; the legal structure; the power of each group. A top-level answer reaches a supported conclusion specific to Atlas Furniture. [10]

items.stem: Which of the following best defines 'compromise'?
options: A stakeholder who is part of the business, such as an employee, manager or owner.
A person or organisation that owns shares in a limited company.
Any individual or group that has an interest in, or is affected by, the activities of a business.
An agreement in which each side gives up part of what it wants in order to settle a conflict.
items.answer: An agreement in which each side gives up part of what it wants in order to settle a conflict.
items.markingKey: compromise: An agreement in which each side gives up part of what it wants in order to settle a conflict. [1]

items.stem: Most of its raw ingredients are imported and paid for in US dollars. Nile Pharma plc, a public limited company in Egypt with about 1,800 employees, manufactures generic medicines for hospitals and pharmacies in Africa and the Middle East. Identify and explain one advantage for Nile Pharma of resolving stakeholder conflict through a compromise.
items.answer: Maintains good relationships; this would help Nile Pharma, which manufactures generic medicines for hospitals and pharmacies in Africa and the Middle East.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: relevant advantage, e.g. maintains good relationships; avoids strikes or boycotts; decisions are more widely accepted. 1 mark: explained in the context of Nile Pharma (pharmaceuticals). [2]

items.stem: Gold Coast Cocoa Ltd is a private limited company based in Accra, Ghana. It buys cocoa from local co-operatives and makes premium chocolate bars and employs about 450 people. World cocoa prices have doubled in eighteen months. Explain one disadvantage to Gold Coast Cocoa of resolving stakeholder conflict through a compromise.
items.answer: No group gets all it wants, which matters for Gold Coast Cocoa because it buys cocoa from local co-operatives and makes premium chocolate bars.
items.markingKey: 1 mark knowledge: a relevant disadvantage, e.g. no group gets all it wants; negotiations take time; may need to be repeated. 1 mark application to Gold Coast Cocoa (confectionery). 1 mark analysis: consequence for the business developed. [3]

items.stem: The owners want to double the number of cafés within three years. Café Cordillera SAS, a private limited company in Colombia with about 900 employees, roasts coffee and runs a chain of 60 cafés. (a) Define the term 'stakeholder conflict'. (b) Evaluate how Café Cordillera should resolve the conflict between its shareholders and its employees.
items.answer: (a) A situation where the objectives of different stakeholder groups cannot all be met at the same time. (b) For: negotiation and compromise; linking pay to productivity; communication of the business situation. Against: shareholders have legal ownership and power; employees may strike; compromise satisfies no one fully. Judgement: for Café Cordillera it depends mainly on the power and interest of each group, and also on the financial position.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark: partial definition; 2 marks: full definition. [2] (b) AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts. AO2 Application [2]: uses the evidence (Café Cordillera: food and drink retail, about 900 employees, private limited company in Colombia; the owners want to double the number of cafés within three years). AO3 Analysis [3]: arguments for, e.g. negotiation and compromise; linking pay to productivity; communication of the business situation; arguments against, e.g. shareholders have legal ownership and power; employees may strike; compromise satisfies no one fully. AO4 Evaluation [3]: a justified judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on the power and interest of each group; the financial position; the long-term objectives. A top-level answer reaches a supported conclusion specific to Café Cordillera. [10]
